Before you decide where it's coming from, ask it what it's trying to stop, or what it wants, or if it just has something to say. It could be your little one, mad that you took so long to come back, or a part of you that's trying to protect you, or the parent you inherited, or something from earlier today, or a bit of each.

guide_passage: Sometimes it is only a thought. Do not create a new inner person every time the mind produces a sentence. Use the least elaborate model that helps. A thought can be labeled “thinking,” allowed to pass, and followed by a return to the room. If it keeps returning with a coherent fear, strategy, age, or demand, a parts dialogue may help. The model serves the person, not the other way around.
next: Once you have a tentative sense of what is present, don’t stop at naming the voices. Notice what each response teaches the others. A loving vow followed by blame when it is doubted teaches something very different from the same vow followed by curiosity. A protector who warns and is heard behaves differently from one that has to become louder because nobody listens. Often the useful insight is in the relationship between the positions, not in the label you give each one.
length: three or four sentences, 50 to 100 words
brief:
- the second paragraph after Joel's pl/ork paragraph, under "Start With Whatever Showed Up", right after the paragraph that ends "or something from earlier today, or a bit of each."
- what it has to carry, in meaning: not every sentence that crosses your mind is somebody. A stray one can be noticed as just thinking and let go, and you come back to the room you're in. But anything that sounds like your little one (young, hurt, mad you were gone) gets heard even the first time, because they learned to hide and may not try twice. A thought that keeps coming back and hangs together, whether it carries a fear, a plan or a demand or sounds like you at a certain age (any one of those is enough), is worth talking to as a part of you. Whatever picture of your insides helps is there for you, not the other way around.
